documents.title: Heightened Import Disclosures for Supply Chain Visibility; Extension of Comment Period
documents.abstract: This document announces that U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) will extend the comment period for an additional 45 days for interested parties to submit comments on the advance notice of proposed rulemaking (ANPRM) regarding supply chain visibility. The ANPRM was published in the Federal Register on September 2, 2026, with comments due on or before December 1, 2026. To allow for as much public participation as possible in the formulation of a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking, CBP is extending the comment period to January 15, 2027.

documents.title: Special Local Regulation; Savannah River, Savannah, GA
documents.abstract: The Coast Guard is establishing a temporary special local regulation (SLR) for the navigable waters of the Savannah River from the Talmadge Bridge to Eastern Wharf. This action is necessary to provide for the safety of life on these navigable waters near Savannah, GA during the Savannah Lighted Boat Parade. This regulation prohibits persons and vessels from entering the regulated area unless specifically authorized by the Captain of the Port Savannah (COTP) or their designated representative.

documents.title: Agricultural Foreign Investment Disclosure Act of 1978
documents.abstract: On June 25, 2026, the United States Department of Agriculture (the Agency) published a proposed rule to update its regulations regarding the Agricultural Foreign Investment Disclosure Act of 1978 (AFIDA) (91 FR 38315) and requested public comment by August 10, 2026. The Agency is reopening the comment period in response to a request from stakeholders to extend the comment period to allow additional time for interested parties to review the proposed revisions and submit comments.

documents.title: Implementation of HAVANA Act of 2021; Correction
documents.abstract: The Department of Justice is correcting a final rule that published in the Federal Register of October 27, 2026, implementing parts of the HAVANA Act of 2021. Due to an editorial error, two instructions were inadvertently combined. This document corrects that error.

documents.title: Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards: Automatic Emergency Braking Systems for Light Vehicles
documents.abstract: NHTSA proposes to modify Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard No. 127; Automatic emergency braking systems for light vehicles. NHTSA proposes to delay the compliance date by two years so that manufacturers have more time to comply with the standard. NHTSA also proposes test procedures for testing the malfunction telltale and to clarify the test speed tolerance. The agency seeks comment on other potential modifications to the standard.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Canada Limited Partnership (Type Certificate Previously Held by C Series Aircraft Limited Partnership (CSALP); Bombardier, Inc.) Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Airbus Canada Limited Partnership Model BD-500-1A10 and BD-500-1A11 airplanes. This AD was prompted by a report of engine stall events that occurred on ground in icing weather conditions (freezing fog) during engine acceleration to take-off thrust, or during the take-off phase. This AD requires revising the existing airplane flight manual (AFM) to provide the flightcrew with a prohibition to follow under certain freezing fog conditions. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Regulations Regarding Payment of Tax by Commercially Acceptable Means; Correction
documents.abstract: This document includes corrections to Treasury Decision 10060 published in the Federal Register on Monday, October 19, 2026. Treasury Decision 10060 contains final regulations regarding the payment of tax by commercially acceptable means.

documents.title: Locatable Minerals
documents.abstract: The U.S. Department of Agriculture, Forest Service (Agency) is reopening the comment period for the proposed rule, "Locatable Minerals," which published in the Federal Register on February 20, 2026 (91 FR 8316). The proposed rule would revise regulations governing occupancy and use of National Forest System lands in connection with prospecting, exploration, development, mining, processing, and reclamation conducted under the mining laws. The Agency is reopening the comment period to allow the public additional time to review the proposed revisions and submit comments. The proposed regulatory text and supporting analyses, including the draft environmental impact statement and cost-benefit analysis are unchanged by this notice.

documents.title: Cost of Living Adjustment to Satellite Carrier Compulsory License Royalty Rates
documents.abstract: The Copyright Royalty Judges ("Judges") announce a cost of living adjustment ("COLA") of 3.9% in the royalty rates satellite carriers pay for a compulsory license under the Copyright Act. The COLA is based on the change in the Consumer Price Index from October 2025 to September 2026.

documents.title: Cost of Living Adjustment to Royalty Rates and Terms for Making and Distributing Phonorecords
documents.abstract: The Copyright Royalty Judges ("Judges") announce a cost of living adjustment ("COLA") in the royalty rates for the statutory license for making and distributing phonorecords of nondramatic musical works regarding physical phonorecords and Permanent Downloads.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Airbus SAS Model A330-202, A330-243, A330-243F, A330-302, A330-323, A330-343, A330-841, and A330-941 airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by an investigation that revealed a potential discrepant gap between the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics (NACA) vent intake panel and horizontal tail plane skin. This proposed AD would require modification of the NACA vent intake panel installation on the horizonal tail plane. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of affected parts. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Bombardier, Inc., Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Bombardier, Inc., Model BD-700-1A10 and BD-700-1A11 airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a report of an issue with the heads-up display application (HDA) software in avionics software version 5.8 that could result in the HDA being unable to read errors in the graphical engine chip (GE5) local and frame buffer memory during power-up. This proposed AD would require installing avionics software version 5.9 or later approved software version. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Reef Fish Fishery of the Gulf of America; Amendment 63
documents.abstract: The Gulf Council (Council) has submitted Amendment 63 to the Fishery Management Plan for the Reef Fish Resources of the Gulf (FMP) (Amendment 63) for review, approval, and implementation by NMFS. If approved, Amendment 63 would, for red grouper in the Gulf of America (Gulf), establish a commercial quota pool under a 3-year pilot program within the Grouper-Tilefish Individual Fishing Quota (IFQ) program. The purpose of Amendment 63 is to test whether a new method of distributing a portion of the red grouper commercial quota improves access to red grouper commercial allocation within the IFQ program, reduces bycatch and discards of IFQ species, and enhances economic profitability for quota pool participants.

documents.title: Security Zone; Ohio River, Cincinnati, OH
documents.abstract: The Coast Guard is establishing a temporary security zone for all navigable waters of the Ohio River, extending the entire width of the river, between mile markers (MM) 461 to MM 473. This security zone is needed to provide waterside security and protection of persons under the protection of the United States Secret Service during a visit to Cincinnati, OH. During the enforcement period, entry into, transiting, or anchoring in the security zone is prohibited unless specifically authorized by the Captain of the Port (COTP), Ohio Valley or a designated on-scene U.S. Coast Guard representative.

documents.title: Exceptional Addressing Changes
documents.abstract: The Postal Service is proposing to amend Mailing Standards of the United States Postal Service, Domestic Mail Manual (DMM[supreg]) in various subsections to eliminate the use of exceptional addressing for Priority Mail, First-Class Mail and USPS Ground Advantage.

documents.title: Fisheries of the Exclusive Economic Zone Off Alaska; Pacific Cod in the Bering Sea Subarea of the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands Management Area
documents.abstract: NMFS is prohibiting directed fishing for Pacific cod, except for the Community Development Quota program (CDQ), in the Bering Sea subarea of the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands management area (BSAI). This action is necessary to prevent exceeding the non-CDQ allocation of the 2026 Pacific cod total allowable catch (TAC) in the Bering Sea subarea of the BSAI.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; General Electric Company Engines
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain General Electric Company (GE) Model GE90-110B1 and GE90- 115B engines. This proposed AD was prompted by a report of an aborted takeoff due to left engine failure caused by liberation of the interstage high-pressure turbine (HPT) rotor seal rim. This proposed AD would require determining the recalculated service life of the interstage HPT rotor seal and, depending on the results, replacing the interstage HPT rotor seal with a part eligible for installation. For certain engine populations, as an alternative to replacing the interstage HPT rotor seal, this proposed AD would require initial and repetitive ultrasonic inspections of the interstage HPT rotor seal for cracks and, depending on the results, removing the interstage HPT rotor seal from service. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Threatened Species Status With Section 4(d) Rule for Ciliate-Leaf Tickseed
documents.abstract: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the ciliate-leaf tickseed (Coreopsis integrifolia), a plant species from Florida, Georgia, and South Carolina as a threatened species with protective regulations under section 4(d) of the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the ciliate- leaf tickseed. After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Plants and extend the Act's protections to the species.

documents.title: Air Quality Plan; California; San Diego County Air Pollution Control District; Landfill Flares
documents.abstract: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is taking final action to conditionally approve a revision to the San Diego County Air Pollution Control District (SDCAPCD or "District") portion of the California State implementation plan (SIP). This revision concerns emissions of oxides of nitrogen (NO<INF>X</INF>) from landfill flares. We are conditionally approving a local rule to regulate these emission sources under the Clean Air Act (CAA or "Act").

documents.title: Technical Updates to the RCRA Hazardous Waste Permitting Regulations-Permitting Technical Updates Rule
documents.abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing technical updates to the regulations implementing the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) governing hazardous waste treatment, storage, and disposal facilities (TSDFs), as well as associated permitting requirements. The proposal also includes a few conforming technical updates to the generator and transporter regulations. The RCRA hazardous waste TSDF permitting regulations have remained largely unchanged for over three decades, despite evolving standards and practices. Collectively, these revisions are intended to address inadvertent errors, remove obsolete references, reflect current information and standards, and implement targeted updates to the RCRA permitting regulations to improve clarity, consistency, and efficiency in the hazardous waste TSDF permitting program. Through a separate Federal Register document, EPA will be seeking input on areas in the RCRA permitting program and permitting regulations to consider for permitting policy or regulatory reform. This proposed rule helps clear the way for potential future regulatory actions that could improve implementation of the RCRA hazardous waste permitting program. It serves as a maintenance action and does not preclude the possibility of future permitting reform.

documents.title: Significant New Use Rule on a Chemical Substance (P-24-195)
documents.abstract: EPA is proposing a significant new use rule (SNUR) under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) for a chemical substance that was the subject of a premanufacture notice (PMN) and is also subject to an Order issued by EPA pursuant to TSCA. The SNUR requires persons to notify EPA at least 90 days before commencing the manufacture (defined by statute to include import) or processing of this chemical substance for an activity that is designated as a significant new use in the SNUR. The required notification initiates EPA's evaluation of the conditions of that use for that chemical substance. In addition, the manufacture or processing for the significant new use may not commence until EPA has conducted a review of the required notification; made an appropriate determination regarding that notification; and taken such actions as required by that determination.

documents.title: Reducing Complexity in Management of Leather Waste
documents.abstract: EPA is proposing to revise the regulations defining solid wastes that are not hazardous wastes by adding a new exclusion. The proposed revision specifies that leather articles used as personal protective equipment are not hazardous wastes when discarded, if they meet the same standards applicable to the currently excluded waste scrap leather from various leather product manufacturing industries.

documents.title: Cost of Living Adjustment to Public Broadcasters Compulsory License Royalty Rate
documents.abstract: The Copyright Royalty Judges ("Judges") announce a cost of living adjustment ("COLA") to the royalty rate that noncommercial radio stations at certain colleges, universities, and other educational institutions that are not affiliated with National Public Radio must pay for the use in 2027 of published nondramatic musical compositions in the SESAC Performing Rights, LLC ("SESAC"), and Global Music Rights, LLC ("GMR"), repertories pursuant to the statutory license under the Copyright Act for noncommercial broadcasting.

documents.title: Air Plan Approval; Virginia; Revision to Minor New Source Review Permit Exemptions
documents.abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing to approve a state implementation plan (SIP) revision (Revision A25) submitted by the Commonwealth of Virginia. This revision pertains to an amendment made in the Virginia Administrative Code (VAC) to include minor New Source Review (NSR) permit exemptions for bovine incinerators for agricultural use. This action is being taken under the Clean Air Act (CAA).

documents.title: Air Plan Approval; Maryland; Interstate Transport Requirements for the 2010 1-Hour Sulfur Dioxide National Ambient Air Quality Standard
documents.abstract: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing to approve portions of a Maryland state implementation plan (SIP) submission as adequate to meet certain Clean Air Act (CAA) interstate transport requirements for the 2010 primary sulfur dioxide (SO<INF>2</INF>) national ambient air quality standard (NAAQS). Specifically, the EPA proposes to find that the SIP submission demonstrates that the Maryland SIP contains adequate provisions prohibiting emissions from Maryland sources from contributing significantly to nonattainment or interfering with maintenance of the 2010 SO<INF>2</INF> NAAQS in any other state. This action is being taken under the CAA.

documents.title: Air Plan Approval; Utah; Cache County Inspection and Maintenance Program Revision
documents.abstract: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing to approve State Implementation Plan (SIP) revisions submitted by the State of Utah on February 28, 2025. The Utah submittal includes revisions to the State's Administrative Rule R307-110-36, concerning SIP Section X Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance (I/M) Program, Part F, Cache County. These revisions updated the rule effectiveness date, updated the definition of vehicle I/M program stations, added emergency vehicle exemptions, and added a part unavailability waiver to the Cache County, Utah I/M program.

documents.title: Air Plan Approval; Texas; Attainment Plan for the Navarro County 2010 Sulfur Dioxide Primary National Ambient Air Quality Standard Nonattainment Area
documents.abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing to approve the State Implementation Plan (SIP) revision that Texas submitted to the EPA on October 24, 2022, for the 2010 1-hour sulfur dioxide (SO<INF>2</INF>) primary national ambient air quality standard (NAAQS) in the Navarro County SO<INF>2</INF> nonattainment area. This SIP (or "attainment plan") includes Texas' attainment demonstration provisions and emissions inventory for the nonattainment area, demonstration of reasonable further progress (RFP), implementation of reasonably available control measures (RACM) (including reasonably available control technology (RACT)), an approved nonattainment new source review (NNSR) program, enforceable emissions limitations and control measures, and adequate contingency measures for the affected area. The EPA is proposing to approve Texas' attainment plan for Navarro County and accompanying provisions for the enforceable control strategy for the Navarro area.

documents.title: Establishment of Class E Airspace; Trading Bay Production Airport, Trading Bay, AK
documents.abstract: This action establishes Class E airspace extending upward from 700 feet above the surface at Trading Bay Production Airport, Trading Bay, AK. This action supports the safety and management of instrument flight rules (IFR) operations at the airport.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain The Boeing Company Model 707 airplanes; Model 720 and 720B series airplanes; Model 727C, 727-100, -100C, -200, and -200F series airplanes; and Model 747-100, -100B, -100B SUD, -200B, -200C, -200F, - 300, 747SR, and 747SP series airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by reports that using some adaptors while performing tests of the cabin altitude warning switch (CAWS) could lead to incorrect failures. This proposed AD would require repetitive operational tests or replacements of the CAWS and applicable on-condition actions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Auction of Flexible-Use Licenses in the Upper C-Band for Next-Generation Wireless Services; Notice and Filing Requirements, Minimum Opening Bids, Upfront Payments, and Other Procedures for Auction 115; Bidding Scheduled To Begin April 27, 2027
documents.abstract: This document summarizes the procedures, deadlines, upfront payment, and minimum opening bid amounts adopted in the Auction 115 Procedures Public Notice for the Federal Communications Commission's (Commission) upcoming auction of 3,248 new flexible-use licenses in the 3.98-4.14 GHz portion of the Upper C-band. The Auction 115 Procedures Public Notice summarized here provides details regarding the procedures, terms, conditions, dates, and deadlines governing participation in Auction 115 bidding, as well as an overview of the post-auction application and payment processes.

documents.title: Safety Zone; Brownsville Ship Channel, Brownsville, TX
documents.abstract: The Coast Guard is establishing a temporary safety zone for navigable waters on the Brownsville Ship Channel. The safety zone is needed to protect personnel, vessels, and the marine environment from potential hazards associated with an over-sized dead ship tow transiting the area. Entry of vessels or persons into this zone is prohibited unless specifically authorized by the Captain of the Port, Sector Corpus Christi, or their designated representative.

documents.title: VIAVI Solutions; Filing of Color Additive Petition
documents.abstract: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or we) is announcing that we have filed a color additive petition, submitted by VIAVI Solutions, proposing that the color additive regulations be amended to provide for the safe use of magnesium fluoride-aluminum flake for use in nail polish at a maximum level of 16 percent of the final product.

agencies.raw_name: DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES
agencies.name: Health and Human Services Department

documents.title: Petition for Rulemaking To Consider Amendments to Regulations Governing Interim Use of Rights-of-Way as Trails
documents.abstract: The Board partially grants a petition for rulemaking and proposes amendments to its regulations implementing section 208 of the National Trails System Act Amendments of 1983 to streamline the railbanking process. Under the proposal, the Board would no longer issue Notices or Certificates of Interim Trail Use during trail-use negotiations. Only after an agreement is reached would the Board issue an order authorizing transfer to the trail sponsor. Abandonment authority would no longer be prerequisite to railbanking. The Board would also confirm that by authorizing transfer the Board is not exercising any power of eminent domain or authorizing a taking.

documents.title: Additions to the Entity List
documents.abstract: In this rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) by adding 7 entities to the Entity List, under the destinations of Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand. These entities have been determined by the U.S. Government to be acting contrary to the national security or foreign policy interests of the United States.

documents.title: Supervisory Committee Audits And Verifications
documents.abstract: The NCUA Board (Board) is amending its regulations governing supervisory committee audits to eliminate unnecessary, redundant, and overly prescriptive provisions. The final rule is necessary to reduce regulatory burden, increase operational flexibility for federally insured credit unions (FICUs), and streamline the rules by removing requirements that are outdated or duplicative of other authorities. The intended effect of the final rule is to simplify compliance for FICUs without compromising the integrity of the audit process.

documents.title: Corporate Credit Unions
documents.abstract: The NCUA Board (Board) is amending its regulations for corporate credit unions by removing the requirement that a corporate credit union's asset and liability management committee (ALCO) must have at least one member who is also a member of the corporate credit union's board of directors. The final rule also removes filing requirements related to a corporate credit union's annual report and any management letter or other report issued by its independent public accountant. The intended effect is to reduce unnecessary regulatory burden and provide corporate credit unions with greater flexibility.

documents.title: Thresholds Increase for the Major Assets Prohibition of the Depository Institution Management Interlocks Act Rule
documents.abstract: The NCUA Board (Board) is issuing a final rule increasing two thresholds in its regulation implementing management official interlocks for purposes of the Depository Institution Management Interlocks Act (DIMIA). DIMIA authorizes NCUA to adjust the major assets prohibition thresholds through regulation to respond to inflation or market changes. This final rule increases both major assets prohibition thresholds to $10 billion to account for changes in the United States banking market since 1996. Additionally, the final rule removes a presumption related to depository institutions controlled or managed by persons who are members of a minority group or women.

documents.title: Fisheries of the Exclusive Economic Zone Off Alaska; Pacific Ocean Perch in the Eastern Aleutian District of the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands Management Area
documents.abstract: NMFS is prohibiting directed fishing for Pacific ocean perch in the Eastern Aleutian district (EAI) of the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands management area (BSAI) by vessels participating in the BSAI trawl limited access sector fishery. This action is necessary to prevent exceeding the 2026 total allowable catch (TAC) of Pacific ocean perch in the EAI allocated to vessels participating in the BSAI trawl limited access sector fishery.

documents.title: Control of Communicable Diseases; Foreign Quarantine
documents.abstract: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), in the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), is extending the expiration date of the interim final rule published on May 27, 2026. This interim final rule removes an exemption for lawful permanent residents from application of regulations implementing section 362 of the Public Health Service (PHS) Act, which authorizes the Secretary, acting through the CDC Director or other delegate, to suspend the introduction of persons from designated countries or places, if required, in the interest of public health.

documents.title: Fisheries of the Exclusive Economic Zone Off Alaska; Atka Mackerel in the Bering Sea Subarea and Eastern Aleutian District of the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands Management Area
documents.abstract: NMFS is prohibiting directed fishing for Atka mackerel in the Bering Sea subarea and Eastern Aleutian District (BS/EAI) of the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands management area (BSAI) by vessels participating in the BSAI trawl limited access sector fishery. This action is necessary to prevent exceeding the 2026 total allowable catch (TAC) of Atka mackerel in the BS/EAI allocated to vessels participating in the BSAI trawl limited access sector fishery.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-19-04, which applies to all Airbus SAS Model A350-941 and -1041 airplanes. AD 2024-19-04 requires a one-time detailed inspection of the engine nacelle anti-icing (NAI) forward bulkhead locating holes for elongation and loose fasteners and applicable corrective actions and prohibits the installation of affected parts under certain conditions. Since the FAA issued AD 2024-19-04, it has been determined that affected parts must accumulate at least 2,000 flight cycles (FC) since installation prior to the inspection to ensure that the inspection will detect discrepancies. This proposed AD would continue to require the actions in AD 2024-19-04 and would amend the compliance time for the inspection. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of affected parts under certain conditions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain The Boeing Company Model 757-200 and -300 series airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a report of missing and/or incorrectly installed lockwire on backshells found during engineering validation tests in the wing leading edge and engine struts for high intensity radiated field (HIRF)/lightning protection features. This proposed AD would require inspection of the backshells at the left- and right-wing leading edge and nacelle strut for missing and incorrectly installed lockwire and applicable on-condition actions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Establishment of Class E Airspace; Canton, TX
documents.abstract: This action proposes to establish Class E airspace at Mother Frances-Canton Heliport, Canton, TX. The FAA is proposing this action to support new instrument procedures and instrument flight rule (IFR) operations.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Canada Limited Partnership (Type Certificate Previously Held by C Series Aircraft Limited Partnership (CSALP); Bombardier, Inc.) Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Airbus Canada Limited Partnership Model BD-500-1A10 and BD-500- 1A11 airplanes. This AD was prompted by a report of multiple in-service failures of pressure regulating shutoff valves (PRSOVs). This AD requires revising the existing airplane flight manual (AFM) to incorporate procedures for reducing the thrust lever or shutting down the engine when the BLEED LEAK caution message is persistent, prohibits operation in known or forecasted icing conditions under certain minimum equipment list (MEL) provisions where the only operative PRSOV is an affected part, and requires replacement of affected PRSOVs with improved PRSOVs. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Endangered Species Status for the Rio Grande Shiner
documents.abstract: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the Rio Grande shiner (Notropis jemezanus), a fish species from the Rio Grande Basin in New Mexico, Texas, and Mexico, as an endangered species under the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the Rio Grande shiner. After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the species. We find that critical habitat for this species is not determinable at this time.

documents.title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Endangered Species Status for Peppered Shiner
documents.abstract: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the peppered shiner (Miniellus perpallidus), a fish species from southeast Oklahoma and southern Arkansas, as an endangered species under the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the peppered shiner. After a review of the best available scientific and commercial information, we find that listing the species is warranted. Accordingly, we propose to list the peppered shiner as an endangered species under the Act. If finalized as proposed, this rule would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the species.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Pilatus Aircraft Ltd. Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2021-11- 08, which applied to all Pilatus Aircraft Ltd. (Pilatus) Model PC-6, PC-6-H1, PC-6-H2, PC-6/350, PC-6/350-H1, PC-6/350-H2, PC-6/A, PC-6/A- H1, PC-6/A-H2, PC-6/B-H2, PC-6/B1-H2, PC-6/B2-H2, PC-6/B2-H4, PC-6/C- H2, and PC-6/C1-H2 airplanes. AD 2021-11-08 required revising the airworthiness limitations section (ALS) of the existing aircraft maintenance manual (AMM) or instructions for continued airworthiness (ICA) to incorporate new airworthiness limitations and adding an additional eddy current inspection of the fuselage wing fittings and wing-to-fuselage fittings if the last inspection was performed using an earlier version of the required material. Since the FAA issued AD 2021- 11-08, the FAA has determined that new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations are necessary. This AD requires revising the ALS of the existing AMM or ICA for these airplanes. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Renaming Narcotic Treatment Program (NTP) to Opioid Treatment Program (OTP) in DEA Regulations
documents.abstract: This final rule updates Drug Enforcement Administration regulations to change the name of Narcotic Treatment Programs to Opioid Treatment Programs. This action is a nomenclature change and makes no substantive changes to the definition of a narcotic drug in the Controlled Substances Act or the definition of a narcotic treatment program in the implementing regulations.

documents.title: Medicare Program; Contract Year 2028 Policy and Technical Changes to the Medicare Advantage Program, Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Program, and Programs of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly
documents.abstract: This proposed rule would revise the Medicare Advantage (Part C), Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit (Part D), and Programs of All- Inclusive Care for the Elderly regulations to implement changes related to marketing and communications, drug coverage, enrollment processes, special needs plans, and other programmatic areas. Additionally, it would establish and implement a mandatory Medicare Advantage (MA) CMS Innovation Center model.

documents.title: Safety Zone; Pasquotank River Harbor, Elizabeth City, NC
documents.abstract: The Coast Guard is establishing a temporary safety zone for certain navigable waters on the Pasquotank River, at Elizabeth City, NC. The safety zone is needed to protect personnel, vessels, and the marine environment from potential hazards associated with an over-the- water drone display. The entry of vessels or persons into this zone is prohibited unless specifically authorized by the Captain of the Port, Sector North Carolina, or their designated representative.

documents.title: Restructuring the Governance and Funding Model of the Consolidated Audit Trail
documents.abstract: Although the consolidated audit trail (the "CAT") continues to be a necessary regulatory tool, its decentralized governance has presented certain challenges to administering the CAT. To address those shortcomings, the Securities and Exchange Commission (the "Commission" or the "SEC") proposes to assume direct control of the CAT. Specifically, the Commission is proposing amendments to Regulation NMS under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 ("Exchange Act") that would rescind Rule 613, which obligates the national securities exchanges and national securities associations (collectively, the "SROs") to act jointly to develop a national market system plan to develop, implement, and maintain the CAT (the "CAT NMS Plan"). The Commission is simultaneously proposing new Rule 17a-26, which would require the SROs and broker-dealers to record and electronically report to a central repository substantially the same information that was previously required to be recorded and reported pursuant to Rule 613, the CAT NMS Plan, related SRO compliance rules, and related exemptive relief previously issued by the Commission.

documents.title: Amendment of Class D Airspace and Class E Airspace Over Tri-Cities, TN
documents.abstract: This action amends Class D and Class E airspace over Tri- Cities, TN. Specifically, this action modifies the Tri-Cities Class D and Class E surface area airspace by expanding the radius and lateral boundaries to the northeast and removing the Tri-Cities Class E surface area extension airspace to the northeast. Additionally, this action modifies the Tri-Cities Class E transitional airspace beginning at 700 feet above the surface by expanding the lateral boundaries of the western portion of the airspace. Lastly, this action updates the airport name within the Class D and E legal descriptions and other outdated verbiage.

documents.title: Loyalty and the Exclusive Purpose Rule in Selecting Plan Investments and Exercising Shareholder Rights
documents.abstract: In this proposed rule, the Department of Labor (Department) clarifies the fiduciary duty of loyalty under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA). The proposed rule affirms that ERISA's duty of loyalty requires fiduciaries to act with the exclusive purpose of ensuring retirement security and providing promised benefits to plan participants and their beneficiaries. The amendments clarify the neutral application of ERISA's fiduciary duties of prudence and loyalty to selecting investments and investment courses of action, and to exercising shareholder rights, including proxy voting, the use of written proxy voting policies and guidelines, and shareholder engagement activities. The amendments would enhance the regulation by adding an affirmative expression of the duty of loyalty that is more consistent with the statute, and removing the tiebreaker test and participant preference provisions, which do not comport with the best reading of the statute and are susceptible to abuse, including use by a fiduciary as pretext to employ plan assets to pursue personal preferences or objectives unrelated to financial benefits under the plan. In the Department's view, the best reading of ERISA's exclusive purpose provision is and has always been that a plan fiduciary may not start with an ulterior motive or consider any factors collateral to plan participants' financial interests during any part of the process of making investment-selection decisions. The proposal would strengthen the fiduciary standards of pension and retirement plans covered by ERISA as instructed in President Trump's Executive Order 14366, Protecting American Investors from Foreign-Owned and Politically Motivated Proxy Advisors.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2026-21- 08, which applied to certain The Boeing Company Model 737-700, -700C, - 800, and -900ER series airplanes. AD 2026-21-08 required a detailed inspection of the left- and right-side form-in-place (FiP) gasket at the engine fuel shutoff valve access panel for correct sealant installation, a fluid leak test of the engine fuel shutoff valve access panels for any leak, and applicable on-condition actions. Since the FAA issued AD 2026-21-08, the FAA has determined that the compliance time exception specified in paragraph (h) of AD 2026-21-08 omits reference to a certain date. This AD retains all of the requirements of AD 2026- 21-08 and adds the omitted reference to the compliance time exception specified in paragraph (h) of this AD. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: International Proof of Delivery Service
documents.abstract: The Postal Service is revising Mailing Standards of the United States Postal Service, International Mail Manual (IMM[supreg]), to reflect changes to product features for Priority Mail International[supreg] (PMI) and to introduce International Proof of Delivery as a new international extra service that will be available for PMI mailpieces to select destinations.

documents.title: IFR Altitudes; Miscellaneous Amendments
documents.abstract: This amendment adopts miscellaneous amendments to the required IFR (instrument flight rules) altitudes and changeover points for certain Federal airways, jet routes, or direct routes for which a minimum or maximum en-route authorized IFR altitude is prescribed. This regulatory action is needed because of changes occurring in the National Airspace System. These changes are designed to provide for the safe and efficient use of the navigable airspace under instrument conditions in the affected areas.

documents.title: Streamlining the Application Process for Grants for Adaptive Sports Programs for Disabled Veterans and Disabled Members of the Armed Forces
documents.abstract: This proposed rule would amend the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) regulations that govern grants for adaptive sports programs for disabled veterans and disabled members of the armed forces to allow for a more efficient review and selection of applicants for the grant. This rule would ensure that the grant aligns with the Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards by requiring applicants to submit an application within the VA established deadline for submission; requiring that all adaptive sports grants be openly competed; and adding a new section on appropriate actions VA may take to enforce this part. The changes proposed by this rulemaking will improve program administration without negatively impacting the veteran athletes supported by these grants.

documents.title: Denial of Rehearing Requests by Operation of Law Under the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure
documents.abstract: The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (Commission) is revising its regulations addressing the circumstances under which a request for rehearing is denied absent Commission action within a particular time frame. Currently, the Commission's regulations provide that unless the Commission acts upon a request for rehearing within 30 days after the request is filed, the request is denied. As revised in this final rule, the regulation will apply only to matters subject to the rehearing and judicial review provisions in the Federal Power Act (FPA) and Natural Gas Act (NGA).

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-10-10, which applies to all Airbus Helicopters Model SA 365 N, SA 365 N1, AS 365 N2, and AS 365 N3 helicopters. AD 2024-10-10 requires a one-time inspection for proper positioning of the tail rotor (TR) actuator harness and cable tie installation and, depending on the results, corrective action. Since the FAA issued AD 2024-10-10, the manufacturer developed a modification to reroute the yaw harness that would apply to certain model helicopters. This proposed AD would retain some of the actions of AD 2024-10-10 and would also require, for certain model helicopters, modifying the helicopter. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters
documents.abstract: The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2025-08-06 which applied to certain Airbus Helicopters Model SA330J helicopters. AD 2025-08-06 required repetitively inspecting for a gap between the main gearbox (MGB) oil cooling fan assembly rotor blade and the upper section of the guide vane bearing housing, replacing the MGB fan rotor bearings with serviceable bearings if necessary, and at a later compliance time replacing the MGB fan rotor bearing assembly with an improved MGB fan rotor bearing assembly, which constitutes terminating action for the repetitive inspections. Since AD 2025-08-06 was issued, the FAA determined that the compliance time for installing the improved MGB fan rotor bearing assembly should be extended. This AD continues to require the actions in AD 2025-08-06 and increases the compliance time for installing the improved MGB fan rotor bearing assembly. This AD also prohibits installing any MGB fan rotor bearings and any MGB fan rotor bearing assembly, unless certain requirements are met. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Bell Textron Canada Limited Helicopters
documents.abstract: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Bell Textron Canada Limited (Bell) Model 429 helicopters. This AD was prompted by reports of premature wear-out of certain spherical bearings due to a quality escape of the spherical bearing monoballs not receiving the required hard coating. This AD requires repetitively inspecting the tail rotor (TR) pitch link assemblies and their bearings for cracks, wear, and mechanical or corrosion damage and, depending on the results, replacing any affected TR pitch link assembly. This AD also allows an affected part to be installed in a helicopter if certain requirements are met. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Helicopters
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2026-08-51, which applies to all Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Model MBB-BK 117 D-3 helicopters. AD 2026-08-51 requires inspecting the rotor hub-shaft for cracks, replacing any rotor hub- shaft that has any crack, and reporting information after accomplishment of the replacement. AD 2026-08-51 also prohibits installing any affected rotor hub-shaft on any helicopter, unless certain requirements are met. Since the FAA issued AD 2026-08-51, it was determined that additional repetitive inspections (including eddy current inspections) are necessary, and that revising the compliance time to account for hoist operations is necessary. This proposed AD would retain the actions of AD 2026-08-51 and would require additional repetitive inspections. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters
documents.abstract: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Airbus Helicopters Model H160-B helicopters. This AD was prompted by a determination that a gap without fire-resistant sealant (sealant) may be present in the cargo bay near the fuel segregation box. This AD requires inspecting for any missing sealant and, depending on findings, corrective action. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Establishment of Class E Airspace Over Hardy, VA
documents.abstract: This action establishes new Class E airspace over Hardy, VA. This airspace is necessary to support Instrument Flight Rules (IFR) operations, utilizing new Special Instrument Approach Procedures (SIAPs) serving Carilion Westlake Center Heliport.

documents.title: Personnel Appeals Board; Procedural Rules
documents.abstract: The Government Accountability Office Personnel Appeals Board (PAB or Board) is amending several significant changes to its existing regulations to streamline and modernize case processing before the Board. The General Accounting Office Personnel Act of 1980 provides authority to make these changes.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; CFM International, S.A. Engines
documents.abstract: The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2018-26-01 for all CFM International, S.A. (CFM) Model CFM56-7B engines. AD 2018- 26-01 required initial and repetitive ultrasonic inspections or eddy current inspections of certain fan blades for crack indications and, depending on the results of the inspections, replacement with parts eligible for installation. Since the FAA issued AD 2018-26-01, CFM issued updated service material providing improvements to the ultrasonic inspection procedures and expanding the inspection area. This AD requires initial and repetitive ultrasonic inspections or eddy current inspections of certain fan blades for crack indications and, depending on the results of the inspections, replacement with parts eligible for installation. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Oil and Gas and Sulfur Operations in the Outer Continental Shelf-Documents Incorporated by Reference
documents.abstract: The Department of the Interior (DOI or Department), through Marine Minerals Administration (MMA), is incorporating by reference a collection of production measurement industry standards and safety industry standards into its regulations governing oil, gas, and sulfur operations on the Outer Continental Shelf (OCS). Incorporation of these documents by reference will provide industry with up-to-date, minimum requirements for measuring oil and gas production volumes and enhancing safety. Compliance with these standards will reduce uncertainty in the measurement of oil and gas production and update the minimum standards in the safety regulations.

documents.abstract: This document announces the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency's (OCC) maximum civil money penalties for 2026 as adjusted for inflation. documents.abstract: This action amends the Class E airspace at Del Rio, TX. This action is the result of a biennial review of the airspace associated with Laughlin Air Force Base (AFB), Del Rio, TX. This action brings the airspace into compliance with FAA orders and supports instrument flight rule (IFR) procedures and operations.

documents.title: Amendment of Class D and E Airspace and Removal of Class E Airspace Over Lebanon, NH
documents.abstract: This action proposes to amend Class D and Class E airspace over Lebanon, NH. This action would increase the lateral dimensions of the Lebanon, NH, Class D airspace to appropriately contain Instrument Flight Rules (IFR) operations at the Lebanon Municipal Airport. This action would also update verbiage in the Class D airspace legal description to comply with current FAA guidance. This action would also update the geographic coordinates for the airport in both the Class D and Class E5 airspace legal descriptions. This action would also remove the exclusions for adjacent Class E5 airspace from the Lebanon, NH, Class E5 airspace legal description. This action would also remove the Lebanon, NH, Class E4 airspace, which is no longer necessary for IFR operations at the airport.

documents.title: Horse Protection Amendments; Extension of Postponement of Regulations
documents.abstract: On May 8, 2024, we published a final rule amending the horse protection regulations. The final rule was initially scheduled to go into effect on February 1, 2025, except for Sec. 11.19, which was effective on June 7, 2024. On January 28, 2025, we published a postponement of the effective date of the remaining provisions from February 1, 2025, to April 2, 2025. On March 21, 2025, we published a further delay of the effective date to February 1, 2026, and a request for comment on whether the length of the postponement should be extended. On January 28, 2026, based on developments following the issuance of the March 21, 2025, delay of effective date, we published a document further delaying the effective date of the final rule to December 31, 2026. On November 13, 2026, we published a proposed rule to remove parts of the 2024 Horse Protection final rule that were vacated by Court order from the regulations, as well as proposing to withdraw the non-vacated parts and update the regulations. As a consequence, in this document, we are issuing an extension of the postponement of the effective date of the final rule to December 31, 2027.

documents.title: Cybersecurity Labeling for Internet of Things
documents.abstract: In this document, the Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau (Bureau) of the Federal Communications Commission (Commission or FCC) seeks comment on recommendations for the U.S. Cyber Trust Mark (USCTM) program, a voluntary cybersecurity labeling program for wireless consumer Internet of Things (IoT) products. The Bureau seeks comment on the design and placement of the FCC IoT Label, display of product registry information, certification renewal, post-market surveillance, and procedures for complaints, noncompliant products, and program administrators that withdraw or whose authority is terminated. These actions would support the establishment and effective administration of the USCTM program and provide consumers with accessible cybersecurity information about certified IoT products.

documents.title: Extension of Import Restrictions Imposed on Archaeological and Ethnological Material of Egypt
documents.abstract: This document amends U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) regulations to reflect the extension of import restrictions on certain categories of archaeological and ethnological material from the Arab Republic of Egypt (Egypt), which were originally published in CBP Decision (CBP Dec.) 16-23, and subsequently extended and amended in CBP Dec. 21-17. documents.abstract: This technical amendment contains non-substantive corrections to address typographical errors, editorial errors, and outdated or incorrect references in various parts of FAA regulations.

documents.title: Employee or Independent Contractor Status Under the Fair Labor Standards Act, Family and Medical Leave Act, and Migrant and Seasonal Agricultural Worker Protection Act
documents.abstract: This final rule rescinds the analysis for determining employee or independent contractor status under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA or Act) set forth in the Department of Labor's (Department) regulations and replaces it with an analysis similar to what it published in a final rule promulgated in 2021, with several modifications and enhancements. In addition, this final rule amends provisions in the Department's regulations implementing the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) and Migrant and Seasonal Agricultural Worker Protection Act (MSPA) to provide that employee or independent contractor status under those laws should be determined using the Department's FLSA analysis, as the FMLA and MSPA both incorporate the FLSA's scope of employment.

documents.title: Regulations Implementing the Privacy Act
documents.abstract: The Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission (OSHRC) is proposing revisions to its regulations implementing the Privacy Act of 1974. The proposed amendments to the Privacy Act regulations provide additional information on how to submit a Privacy Act request and revise the requirements for verifying a requester's identity.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; ATR-GIE Avions de Transport Régional Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all ATR-GIE Avions de Transport R[eacute]gional Model ATR42 and ATR72 airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a review of mooring loads that revealed that winds within the currently defined wind profiles could lead to loads exceeding the certification limits on the nose landing gear (NLG) and main landing gear (MLG) while the airplane is moored. This proposed AD would require revising the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate a revised maintenance procedure (MP) for mooring the airplane. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; ATR-GIE Avions de Transport Régional Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all ATR-GIE Avions de Transport R[eacute]gional Model ATR42-500 and ATR72-212A airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by reports of two in-service events during takeoff where an internal failure of the integrated air system control (IASC) software analog-to-digital converter generated erroneous pressure digital values, leading to uncommanded full-speed closure of the outflow valve and a high negative cabin altitude rate. This proposed AD would require installing improved IASC software. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of affected software under certain conditions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Updates and Amendments to the Civil Service Rules
documents.abstract: The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) is confirming the effective date of the direct final rule updating and amending obsolete and outdated provisions of the Civil Service Rules. OPM received no significant adverse comments and therefore confirms that the direct final rule became effective as scheduled.

documents.title: Procedures for Settling Claims
documents.abstract: The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) confirms that the direct final rule updating the procedures for submitting certain administrative claims to OPM became effective as scheduled.

documents.title: FLSA Claims and Compliance
documents.abstract: The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) confirms that the direct final rule updating provisions concerning Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) claims submissions to OPM became effective as scheduled.

documents.title: Federal Employees' Retirement System; Present Value Conversion Factors for Spouses of Deceased Separated Employees
documents.abstract: The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) is confirming the effective date of its direct final rule revising the table of reduction factors for early commencing dates of survivor annuities paid to spouses of separated employees who die before the date on which they would be eligible for unreduced deferred annuities. OPM received no significant adverse comments during the comment period and confirms the rule was effective August 24, 2026.

documents.title: Extension of Import Restrictions Imposed on Archaeological and Ethnological Material of Greece
documents.abstract: This document amends U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) regulations to reflect the extension of import restrictions on certain categories of archaeological and ecclesiastical ethnological material from the Hellenic Republic (Greece), which were originally published in CBP Decision (Dec.) 11-25 on December 1, 2011, and subsequently extended in 2016, and amended and extended in 2021 in CBP Dec. 21-16. The CBP regulations are being amended to reflect this further extension through November 21, 2031.

documents.title: Implementation of HAVANA Act of 2021
documents.abstract: This rule provides implementation by the Department of Homeland Security ("the Department" or "DHS") of the HAVANA Act of 2021. The HAVANA Act provides authority for agency heads to provide payments to certain individuals who have incurred qualifying injuries to the brain. This rule covers current and former Department of Homeland Security employees and their dependents.

documents.title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Threatened Species Status With Section 4(d) Rule for White Sands Pupfish and Critical Habitat Determination
documents.abstract: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the White Sands pupfish (Cyprinodon tularosa), a fish species from southcentral New Mexico, as a threatened species with protective regulations under section 4(d) of the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the White Sands pupfish. After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the species. All areas meeting the definition of critical habitat for the White Sands pupfish occur on Department of War (DoW) owned facilities and are exempt from designation as critical habitat in accordance with section 4(a)(3)(B) of the Act. Therefore, we are not proposing any areas as critical habitat for the White Sands pupfish.

documents.title: Magnuson-Stevens Act Provisions; Fisheries Off West Coast States; Pacific Coast Groundfish Fishery; 2026 Tribal Fishery Allocations for Pacific Whiting; Reapportionment Between Tribal and Non-Tribal Sectors
documents.abstract: This document announces the reapportionment of 29,130 metric tons of Pacific whiting from the Tribal allocation to the non-Tribal commercial fishery sectors via automatic actions on September 14, and 23, and October 5, 2026. This reapportionment is to allow full utilization of the Pacific whiting resource.

documents.title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Endangered Species Status for Mazama Newt
documents.abstract: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the Mazama newt (Taricha granulosa mazamae), an amphibian species from the Crater Lake caldera in Crater Lake National Park in Klamath County, Oregon, as an endangered species under the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the Mazama newt. After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the species. We find that designating critical habitat for this species is not determinable at this time.

documents.title: Petition for Rulemaking of Alden Graham
documents.abstract: Please take notice that the Federal Trade Commission ("Commission") received a petition for rulemaking from Alden Graham and has published that petition online at https://www.regulations.gov. The Commission invites written comments concerning the petition. documents.title: Special Local Regulations; Annual Marine Events on the Colorado River, Between Davis Dam (Bullhead City, Arizona) and Headgate Dam (Parker, Arizona), BlueWater Resort and Casino Thanksgiving Regatta, Colorado River, Parker, AZ
documents.abstract: The Coast Guard will enforce special local regulations for the BlueWater Resort and Casino Thanksgiving Regatta from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. on November 26, 2026, through 28, 2026, to provide for the safety of life on navigable waterways during this event. Our regulation for marine events within the Southwest Coast Guard District identifies the regulated area for this event in Parker, AZ. During the enforcement periods, the operator of any vessel in the regulated area must comply with directions from the Patrol Commander or any Official Patrol displaying a Coast Guard ensign.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain The Boeing Company Model 737-600, -700, -700C, -800, and -900 series airplanes. This AD was prompted by a review of the autothrottle (A/T) cruise thrust split monitor (MONFD) and the determination that there is a potential for latent loss of spoiler sensor position data or erroneous spoiler sensor position data. This AD requires repetitive aileron built-in test equipment (BITE) tests of the digital flight control system and applicable on-condition actions. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Airbus SAS Model A330-841 and A330-941 airplanes. This AD was prompted by a report of cracks on the discharge outlet of certain engine fire extinguisher bottles. This AD requires modification of affected fire extinguisher bottles and prohibits the installation of affected parts. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Air Plan Approval; Oklahoma; Update to Materials Incorporated by Reference
documents.abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is updating the materials that are incorporated by reference (IBR) into the Oklahoma State Implementation Plan (SIP). The regulations affected by this update have been previously submitted by the State of Oklahoma and approved by the EPA. This update affects the materials that are available for public inspection at the EPA Regional Office and the National Archives and Records Administration.

documents.title: Cotton Board Rules and Regulations: Adjusting Supplemental Assessment on Imports (2025 Amendments)
documents.abstract: The Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) is amending the Cotton Board Rules and Regulations to decrease the value assigned to imported cotton for the purposes of calculating supplemental assessments collected for use by the Cotton Research and Promotion Program. This amendment is required each year to ensure that assessments collected on imported cotton, and the cotton content of imported products, will be the same as those paid on domestically produced cotton. In addition, AMS is updating the Import Assessment Table to account for changes since the last assessment adjustment in 2024.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all The Boeing Company Model 757 airplanes. This AD was prompted by reports of crack damage at existing reinforcing repairs in the fuselage frame lower lobe areas in certain sections. This AD requires doing an inspection for any existing reinforcing repairs in the fuselage frame lower lobe areas in certain sections and applicable on-condition actions. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Air Plan Approval; Arkansas; Update to Materials Incorporated by Reference
documents.abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is updating the materials that are incorporated by reference (IBR) into the Arkansas State Implementation Plan (SIP). The regulations affected by this update have been previously submitted by the State of Arkansas and approved by the EPA. This update affects the materials that are available for public inspection at the EPA Regional Office and the National Archives and Records Administration.

documents.title: Air Plan Approval; Kentucky; Campbell-Clermont Area Maintenance Plan for the 2010 1-Hour SO2 NAAQS; Withdrawal of Direct Final Rule
documents.abstract: Due to the receipt of adverse comments, the U.S Environmental Protection Agency (EPA or Agency) is withdrawing the September 25, 2026, direct final rule that approved the second 10-year maintenance plan for the Kentucky portion of the Campbell-Clermont, Kentucky-Ohio maintenance area ("Campbell-Clermont, KY-OH Area" or "Area") for the 2010 1- hour sulfur dioxide (SO<INF>2</INF>) National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS).

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters
documents.abstract: The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2025-13- 09, which applied to all Airbus Helicopters Model AS-365N2, AS 365 N3, EC 155B, EC155B1, SA-365N, and SA-365N1 helicopters. AD 2025-13-09 required inspecting the tightening torque, reporting the results of the inspections, and, depending on the results of the inspection, taking corrective action. Since the FAA issued AD 2025-13-09, the manufacturer determined that additional inspections of the main rotor (MR) servo-controls nut torque are required. This AD retains some of the actions of AD 2025-13-09 and requires additional inspections and, depending on the results of the inspection, corrective actions. This AD also requires reporting certain information to the manufacturer. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Reef Fish Fishery in the Gulf of America; 2026 Recreational Private Angling Component Closure for Red Snapper in Federal Waters off Texas
documents.abstract: NMFS closes the 2026 recreational fishing season for the red snapper private angling component in Federal waters of the Gulf of America (Gulf) off Texas. The recreational private angling component in Federal waters off Texas is closed on November 21, 2026, and this closure continues through the remainder of 2026. This red snapper closure is necessary to prevent the private angling component from exceeding the annual catch limit (ACL) in the Texas regional management area and to prevent overfishing of red snapper.

documents.title: Periodic Reporting
documents.abstract: The Commission is acknowledging a recent Postal Service filing requesting the Commission initiate a rulemaking proceeding to consider changes to analytical principles relating to periodic reports. This document informs the public of the filing, invites public comment, and takes other administrative steps.

documents.title: Unleashing the Power of Unlicensed Ultra-Wideband Devices; Petition of Robert Bosch LLC for Amendment of the Part 15 Subpart F Ultra-Wideband Rules; and Petition of Alliance for Automative Innovation et al. To Amend Part 15 of the FCC's Rules To Permit the Operation of Certain Ultra-Wideband Devices
documents.abstract: The Federal Communications Commission (Commission or FCC) proposes to update its rules for Ultra-Wideband (UWB) devices to reflect significant technological developments since the rules were first adopted in 2002. UWB technology has matured into a widely used, low-power enabler that supports applications in tracking, automation, precision location, health monitoring, athletic performance, and public safety. As capabilities of UWB have expanded, the existing rules have not kept pace with the technological change, resulting in an increasing number of waiver requests received by the Commission to authorize modern devices. The Notice of Proposed Rulemaking seeks comment on revisions intended to modernize the UWB framework, provide greater flexibility for future applications, promote continued innovation, and ensure the protection of incumbent federal and non-federal spectrum users.

documents.title: Significant New Use Rules on Certain Chemical Substances (26-7)
documents.abstract: EPA is proposing significant new use rules (SNURs) under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) for certain chemical substances that were the subject of premanufacture notices (PMNs) and are also subject to an Order issued by EPA pursuant to TSCA. Once finalized, the SNURs would require persons who intend to manufacture (defined by statute to include import) or process any of these chemical substances for an activity that is proposed as a significant new use by this rulemaking to notify EPA at least 90 days before commencing that activity. The required notification initiates EPA's evaluation of the conditions of that use for that chemical substance. In addition, the manufacture or processing for the significant new use may not commence until EPA has conducted a review of the required notification, made an appropriate determination regarding that notification, and taken such actions as required by that determination.

documents.title: Safety Standard for Automatic Residential Garage Door Operators
documents.abstract: In October 2025, updates to the entrapment protection provisions in the UL 325 standard were accepted under the Consumer Product Safety Improvement Act of 1990 (Improvement Act) for inclusion in the Commission's mandatory safety regulation for automatic residential garage door operators. In this direct final rule, the Consumer Product Safety Commission (Commission) is amending the Commission's automatic residential garage door operators mandatory regulation to align with the changes in UL 325.

documents.title: Schedules of Controlled Substances: Placement of Centanafadine in Schedule III
documents.abstract: On July 24, 2026, the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved a new drug application for Simtriyo (centanafadine) for the treatment of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder in adults and pediatric patients aged 6 years and older, weighing at least 20 kg. The Department of Health and Human Services provided the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) with a scheduling recommendation to place centanafadine, chemically known as (1R,5S)-1- (naphthalen-2-yl)-3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane, in schedule III of the Controlled Substances Act (CSA). In accordance with the CSA, as amended by the Improving Regulatory Transparency for New Medical Therapies Act, DEA is hereby issuing an interim final rule placing centanafadine, including its salts, isomers (whether optical, positional, or geometric), and salts of such isomers whenever the existence of such salts, isomers, and salts of isomers is possible in schedule III of the CSA.

documents.title: Reducing Bureaucracy and Burden for Block Grants
documents.abstract: ACF proposes to amend its block grant regulations to modernize requirements, reduce administrative burden on States and Tribal grantees, and improve the clarity and efficiency of program administration. The current regulations include outdated provisions and procedural requirements that no longer reflect statutory authority or agency practice. The proposed revisions are intended to streamline grantee obligations, eliminate unnecessary requirements, and align the regulations with current law and policy.

documents.title: Air Plan Approval and Air Quality Designation; TN; Attainment Plan and Redesignation of the Sullivan County Nonattainment Area for the 2010 1-Hour Primary SO2 NAAQS
documents.abstract: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA or Agency) is proposing to approve the State of Tennessee's attainment plan for the Sullivan County Nonattainment Area (Sullivan County Area or Area) for the 2010 Sulfur Dioxide (SO<INF>2</INF>) National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS). Additionally, the EPA is proposing to determine that the Area has attained the 2010 SO<INF>2</INF> NAAQS and to approve Tennessee's maintenance plan for continued attainment. With these approvals, the EPA is proposing to approve Tennessee's comprehensive source-specific SO<INF>2</INF> permitted limits for two facilities in the Area, other control measures, and provisions for Reasonably Available Control Measures (RACM) and Reasonably Available Control Technology (RACT), reasonable further progress (RFP), a modeling demonstration of SO<INF>2</INF> attainment and maintenance, and to approve Tennessee's request to redesignate the Area from nonattainment to attainment of the 2010 SO<INF>2</INF> NAAQS. The EPA is taking these actions in accordance with the Clean Air Act (CAA or Act).

documents.title: Air Plan Approval; California; Reasonable Further Progress Plan for the Coachella Valley Ozone Nonattainment Area
documents.abstract: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA or "the Agency") is proposing to approve a state implementation plan (SIP) revision from the State of California to meet the Clean Air Act (CAA) "Extreme" nonattainment area requirements for the Riverside County (Coachella Valley), California ozone nonattainment area ("Coachella Valley") for the 2008 8-hour ozone national ambient air quality standards (NAAQS or "standards"). Specifically, the Agency is proposing to approve the reasonable further progress (RFP) demonstration and associated emissions inventory and motor vehicle emissions budgets ("budgets") for the Coachella Valley.

documents.title: Safety Zone; Southern California Annual Firework Events for the Los Angeles-Long Beach Captain of the Port Zone
documents.abstract: The Coast Guard is proposing to amend the Southern California Firework Events for Los Angeles-Long Beach Captain of the Port Zone Annual Safety Zones. The Coast Guard proposes eight new events to be added, thirteen events to be updated, and two events removed. The safety zones are needed to protect waterways users and keep them clear of potentially harmful debris within the fallout zone. This proposed rulemaking would prohibit persons and vessels from being in the safety zone unless specifically authorized by the Captain of the Port Los Angeles-Long Beach. We invite your comments on this proposed rulemaking.

documents.title: Special Conditions: Embraer S.A. Model ERJ 190-400 Airplane; Embraer Enhanced Takeoff System
documents.abstract: This action proposes special conditions for the Embraer S.A. (Embraer) Model ERJ 190-400 series airplane. This airplane will have a novel or unusual design feature when compared to the state of technology envisioned in the airworthiness standards for transport category airplanes. This design feature is a functionality known as the Embraer Enhanced Takeoff System (E\2\TS). The applicable airworthiness regulations do not contain adequate or appropriate safety standards for this design feature. These proposed special conditions contain the additional safety standards that the Administrator considers necessary to establish a level of safety equivalent to that established by the existing airworthiness standards.

documents.title: Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act, Exchange Pre-Eligibility Verification
documents.abstract: This proposed rule would implement new requirements specified under the Working Families Tax Cut (WFTC) legislation related to Exchange eligibility and verification. This proposed rule contains related updates to provisions affecting inconsistency periods, inconsistency verification procedures, annual eligibility redeterminations and eligibility redeterminations during the plan year, as well as expanding enrollment methods during the verification process and establishing new coverage effective dates.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; CFM International, S.A. Engines
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all CFM International, S.A. (CFM) Model CFM56-7B engines. This proposed AD was prompted by an event involving a CFM Model CFM56-7B26/3 engine where a fan blade separated and resulted in an engine in-flight shutdown (IFSD) with debris penetrating the fuselage, which caused a loss of pressurization and prompted an emergency descent. This proposed AD would require a visual inspection of the fan blades for findings considered not serviceable and, depending on the results of the inspection, replacement with a serviceable part and additional fan blade inspections. This proposed AD would also require sending the inspection results to CFM if any finding considered not serviceable is found. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
